extraction.name: LUMA: A Benchmark Dataset for Learning from Uncertain and Multimodal Data
extraction.description: LUMA is a multimodal benchmark dataset featuring audio, image, and textual data from 50 classes, designed for learning from uncertain data. It extends CIFAR-10/100 with audio samples from three audio corpora and text generated using Gemma-7B LLM. It includes 101,000 images, 135,096 speech audio recordings, and 62,875 text passages (~3 GB). A Python toolkit enables controlled injection of aleatoric and epistemic uncertainties per modality.
extraction.creator: Grigor Bezirganyan, Sana Sellami, Laure Berti-Équille, Sébastien Fournier (Aix Marseille Univ, CNRS, LIS; IRD, ESPACE-DEV)
extraction.citeAs: Grigor Bezirganyan, Sana Sellami, Laure Berti-Équille, and Sébastien Fournier. 2025. LUMA: A Benchmark Dataset for Learning from Uncertain and Multimodal Data. In Proceedings of the 48th International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval (SIGIR '25), July 13–18, 2025, Padua, Italy. ACM, New York, NY, USA, 10 pages. https://doi.org/10.1145/3726302.3730302
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Images were sourced from CIFAR-10/100 (with EDM-generated augmentations). Audio samples were extracted from three corpora: The Spoken Wikipedia, LibriSpeech, and Mozilla Common Voice, plus 73 voluntary recordings from colleagues. Text passages were generated using the Gemma-7B Instruct LLM with 13 different prompts per class label.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Web Scraping, Software Collection, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Some audio classes had fewer than 600 validated samples after automatic and manual validation; these were designated as OOD classes rather than in-distribution classes.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images: CIFAR-10/100 dataset and EDM-generated images. Audio: The Spoken Wikipedia, LibriSpeech, Mozilla Common Voice corpora, and 73 voluntary colleague recordings. Text: Generated by Gemma-7B Instruct LLM using 13 prompts per class label.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The Python toolkit allows injection of aleatoric and epistemic uncertainties via: (1) data diversity control using inverse-distance sampling with parameter k; (2) sample noise injection (background noise for audio, keyboard/OCR/random/antonym/word/spelling/back-translation noise for text, 15 perturbation types for images); (3) label noise injection by reassigning labels to semantically closest class; (4) OOD sample injection from held-out classes.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Audio: forced alignments used to extract word-level segments; automatic validation with OpenAI Whisper Large V3; manual validation via Label Studio for samples failing automatic validation. Text: label occurrences masked and fed back to Gemma-7B for classification validation; bias detection and prompt reconstruction for 4 biased classes. Images: 42 classes with ≥600 samples selected as in-distribution; 8 classes as OOD.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Manual validation of audio samples was performed by colleagues (M.Sc. and PhD students, and professors) with advanced to fluent English knowledge. Annotators were shown the audio sample and asked 'Is the audio saying the word below? (An extra 's' or 'es' in the pronunciation is okay.)' with Yes/No options. Two annotations were collected per sample; samples where both annotators confirmed validity were accepted; conflicting annotations were rejected.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: 71.61% annotation agreement was achieved. Samples where both annotators confirmed validity were accepted (5,027 samples). Samples with conflicting annotations were rejected. Automatic validation (Whisper Large V3) was used first; manual validation was only performed for samples failing automatic validation.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: 17 annotators: M.Sc. and PhD students, and professors with advanced to fluent English knowledge
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: OpenAI Whisper Large V3 (audio transcription for automatic validation); Gemma-7B Instruct (text validation and bias detection)
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset can be easily extended with additional modalities and augmented with more data samples. Future plans include adding dependent modalities.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: 73 audio recordings voluntarily contributed by colleagues were anonymized before inclusion.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset contains gender-biased text for classes 'man', 'woman', 'boy', and 'girl', generated by the LLM. The authors acknowledge this and attempted to mitigate it through prompt reconstruction, but note that significant bias remains. The dataset is not intended as a source of knowledge or information.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Gender bias was detected in text generated for classes 'man', 'woman', 'boy', and 'girl'. The Gemma-7B model was used to detect gender, racial, religious, and cultural biases. Prompts were reconstructed for these 4 classes to reduce bias, but significant bias remains. The authors note that LLMs trained on unbalanced data tend to produce biased descriptions of gendered terms.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Audio samples from forced alignments may contain misaligned segments introducing noise. Voluntary audio contributions may include very noisy samples or strong accents. Text generated by LLM may contain factual inaccuracies or biases. LUMA shall not be used as a source of knowledge or information. The dataset currently lacks dependent modalities.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking multimodal deep learning algorithms on uncertain data; evaluating uncertainty quantification methods (aleatoric and epistemic); OOD detection; studying model robustness to noise; training, testing, and validation of multimodal classification models.

name.evidence: We propose LUMA, a unique multimodal dataset, featuring audio, image, and textual data from 50 classes, specifically designed for learning from uncertain data.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: We compiled the images from the CIFAR 10/100 dataset, extracted, validated, and associated audio samples corresponding to the CIFAR image class labels from three diverse audio corpora, and generated the text modality based on the class labels using the Gemma-7B Instruct Large Language Model (LLM).

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: For the image modality, our priority was to choose a relatively simple yet well-known dataset... we used The Spoken Wikipedia, LibriSpeech, and Mozilla Common Voice corpora... we decided to employ a generative model, and generate text segments about the class label.

rai:dataCollectionMissingData.evidence: We took another 8 classes, which had less than 600 samples after aligning with other modalities, as OOD samples.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: We compiled the images from the CIFAR 10/100 dataset, extracted, validated, and associated audio samples corresponding to the CIFAR image class labels from three diverse audio corpora [The Spoken Wikipedia, LibriSpeech, and Mozilla Common Voice], and generated the text modality based on the class labels using the Gemma-7B Instruct Large Language Model (LLM).

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: We prioritized flexibility, offering multiple options for controlling uncertainty through adjustable parameters such as data diversity, sample-level noise, label corruption, and the injection of out-of-distribution (OOD) samples.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: The automatic validation was achieved with the OpenAI's Whisper Large V3 model for audio transcription... To validate that the generated texts accurately represent the labels, we masked all label occurrences in the text and fed the masked text back into the Gemma-7B Instruct model, asking it to classify the text into one of the labels.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: We asked our colleagues (M.Sc. and PhD students, and professors) with advanced to fluent English knowledge to annotate the samples. In total, we collected 2 annotations per sample, from 17 annotators. We got 71.61% annotation agreement and accepted 5,027 samples, where both annotators confirmed the validity of the sample. Samples with conflicting annotations were rejected.

rai:dataAnnotationPlatform.evidence: We opted for Label Studio to build the labeling interface.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: In total, we collected 2 annotations per sample, from 17 annotators. We got 71.61% annotation agreement and accepted 5,027 samples, where both annotators confirmed the validity of the sample. Samples with conflicting annotations were rejected.

rai:annotationsPerItem.evidence: In total, we collected 2 annotations per sample, from 17 annotators.

rai:annotatorDemographics.evidence: We asked our colleagues (M.Sc. and PhD students, and professors) with advanced to fluent English knowledge to annotate the samples. In total, we collected 2 annotations per sample, from 17 annotators.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: The automatic validation was achieved with the OpenAI's Whisper Large V3 model for audio transcription... To validate that the generated texts accurately represent the labels, we masked all label occurrences in the text and fed the masked text back into the Gemma-7B Instruct model, asking it to classify the text into one of the labels.

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: The dataset can be easily extended with additional modalities and augmented with more data samples. In the future, we plan to include dependent modalities, enabling more comprehensive studies of uncertainty quantification as well as improved applicability in information retrieval contexts.

rai:personalSensitiveInformation.evidence: 73 additional recordings of pronunciations belonging to 4 classes ('roses', 'telephone', 'whale', 'wolf') were voluntarily contributed by our colleagues, which were anonymized, trimmed, and added to the dataset.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: Since textual data was generated using an LLM, we recognize that the dataset may contain factual inaccuracies, or biases, but our aim is to offer a benchmark to study uncertainty quantification in multimodal classification settings. LUMA shall not be used as a source of knowledge or information.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: Particularly, we noticed a lots of gender bias for classes 'man', 'woman', 'boy' and 'girl'. To find the proportion of the biased data, we asked the Gemma model to find out if the given text contains gender, racial, religious, or cultural biases.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: Since most of the audio data is collected from forced alignments, it is possible to have misaligned audio segments, which could introduce additional noise to the dataset... Since textual data was generated using an LLM, we recognize that the dataset may contain factual inaccuracies, or biases... LUMA shall not be used as a source of knowledge or information.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: This comprehensive dataset and its tools are intended to promote and support the development, evaluation, and benchmarking of trustworthy and robust multimodal deep learning approaches. We anticipate that the LUMA dataset will help the research community to design more trustworthy and robust machine learning approaches for safety critical applications.
